correctness.rationale: John uniqueness forces horizontal reflection symmetry and zero shear; every section is homothetic to the base. Replacing its horizontal ellipsoid with the scaled John ellipsoid is volume improving unless already optimal. Inclusion is equivalent to two sharp support-circle inequalities; their sum constrains the two axial scales. The resulting smooth one-dimensional objective has a unique global maximum because XY/t² strictly decreases from infinity to one, and its exact quartic has one positive root. Strict convexity of each square-root term with respect to the apex height, at positive scales, proves the strict height-imbalance order. Symmetric and limiting cone values and the constant host volume follow by exact substitution/integration. The standalone Python verifier passed 6,132 sample checks, which do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A motivated natural convex-body family has a complete unique optimizer for arbitrary centrally symmetric bases. The nontrivial horizontal-shape universality, analytic shape-independent axial parameters, constant-host-volume strict order under apex imbalance, sharp limiting factor, and √d growth quantify an extremal approximation phenomenon across all dimensions. The result is not a routine isolated numeric evaluation or already-stated single-cone specialization.
